content:
In June this year, we noted three instances involving applications from clients of a US-sanctioned Russian bank bypassing the App Store review process to get published. Two months later, another example reached the top of the iPhone App Store.

"K8CHEN PRO" is the latest case. The App Store listing disguises it as an augmented reality (AR)-driven kitchen design application.

Once opened, the application quickly 'strips off' the disguise. The privacy policy link shown on the App Store is allegedly auto-generated by 'Free Privacy Policy Generator' — which in itself may already be a warning sign.

Either way, this application is unmistakably a client application for T-Bank. What is interesting is how these applications can repeatedly pass App Store review.

When it gains enough exposure and climbs to a high position on the App Store charts, the situation becomes obvious — they simply should not be there. It is quite baffling.

Other cases mentioned in June can be found here and here.

Update: Sure enough, the application has already been removed from the App Store.
